subject: SLO deviation: production latency — compensation and trial extension
messages:
From: Tina Park <tina@brightbuy.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightbuy.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike — request for compensation and trial extension

Sean —

We're seeing repeated latency regressions against our production routes since the 02:00 PST deploy window (requests timing out or stalling at 800-1,200ms for simple chat completions). This has affected two of our high-traffic features and rolled back conversions for our beta users. Support ticket #53217 has the traces attached.

We appreciate Redwood's responsiveness on the ticket, but given the customer impact and the fact that we were within our committed SLO, we'd like to discuss a goodwill compensation package (credits) and a 30-day extension of our trial window while we validate the fixes. Please let me know what is possible from your side — we need something concrete to present to our execs.

Attaching the latency CSV and a couple of screenshots.

Thanks,
Tina Park
Director of Product, BrightBuy
T: (415) 555-0198

Attachments: latency_report_20260302.csv (csv), screenshot_error_500.png (png)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Tina Park <tina@brightbuy.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightbuy.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — request for compensation and trial extension

Hi Tina —

First, I'm sorry BrightBuy ran into this. I can confirm the team traced the regression to a kernel mismatch in our autoscaler that increased tail latency for a small subset of traffic between 02:00–03:15 PST. We've patched the issue and rolled a rollback; you should see normalized tail latency in the ticket traces.

As a next step I want to make this right: I'm opening this for escalation internally and proposing a provisional offer of 50k token credits + a 30-day trial extension while we run verification with your QA team. I need approval for the promo from my manager and finance (copying you on the timeline). If that's acceptable as an interim proposal, I'll come back with an exact credit bucket and confirm when the credit posts to your account.

I'll also share the postmortem link once we finalize it. Thank you for the detailed traces — that was really helpful.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Forwarding BrightBuy's escalation. Summary: post-deploy latency regression impacted production for ~75 minutes (ticket 53217). Customer is asking for credits + 30-day trial extension while they validate fixes. Proposed interim offer: 50k token credits + 30 days (we can scale back if needed).

Notes and asks:
- BrightBuy is on a mid-size ARR pipeline (deal BB-1891). They are in active evaluation; customer success sees expansion potential.
- Costed estimate for 50k token credit is ~ $650 list cost.
- Precedent: we issued ~30k credits in Q4 for a similar SLO deviation to retain the account.

Please advise whether we can approve the full 50k + 30d extension as a one-off. If you prefer, approve a smaller amount (30k + 14d) and I'll communicate immediately. If approved, Tessa — please follow billing ops/process to post the promotional credit and update HubSpot (link below).

Thanks for the context. Approve a mitigated relief package: 30,000 token credits + a 14-day trial extension. Please tag the billing entry as "SLO-comp relief" and include the support ticket ID for audit.

Rationale: preserves margin while acknowledging customer impact. If BrightBuy escalates beyond this or signals churn intent, escalate back to me and we'll discuss further.

—Evelyn
